My land is about 10 mu in total. My family has always planted wheat in the autumn and maize in the summer — that's what everyone around here does, and that's what my parents taught me. I don't think too hard about changing things. The wheat-maize rotation keeps the soil okay and we know how to sell both at the local market or to the grain station.

For wheat, I'll plant after the maize harvest in October, before it gets too cold. I'll buy the improved seeds from the village cooperative — those have been around for years and my neighbors all use them. My father-in-law always said to water the wheat four times: once before winter sets in, once when it starts jointing, once when it heads, and once when the grain is filling. I follow that. For fertilizer, I put down a base application when I plant and then top-dress with urea in the spring. I spray for aphids and powdery mildew — those always show up. I use the rotary tiller to prepare the bed before planting.

For summer maize, I'll sow right after the wheat harvest in June, straight into the stubble — no time to plough in summer, the ground is hot and I need to get the seeds in quickly. I use hybrid seeds from the local agri-store, the kind with the yellow bag. Rain usually helps with irrigation in summer, so I only water if the weather turns dry. I spray once or twice for corn borer.

I won't try vegetables this year — last year I grew some on a small patch but the market price dropped and it wasn't worth the extra work with two kids at home.

decision.reasoning_summary: I farm 10 mu in Quzhou County following the winter wheat and summer maize rotation my family has practiced for generations. I plant improved wheat varieties in October using rotary tillage, irrigating four times across the season and applying nitrogen and phosphorus at rates consistent with local custom, spraying three times for common pests and disease. After the wheat harvest in June I direct-seed hybrid maize into the stubble without tillage to save time, relying mostly on summer rainfall with two supplemental irrigations and two pesticide applications for corn borer. I chose not to grow vegetables this year after a poor return last season. My decisions are guided by what my parents taught me and what my neighbors do.
